newsitem.title: UK: FUND VIEW - F&C sows seed money with new Russia fund.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - F&C sows seed money with new Russia fund.

text.p: Foreign and Colonial said its new Russia fund gives investors a highly flexible alternative for one of the world's last big emerging economies, adding that investors can expect liquidity to drive prices higher this year.

"We expect to see a liquidity-driven (market) rally in the autumn...and in 1997 we expect a resumption of GDP growth -- you could see multiple returns for blue chip companies," said Isabel Knight, manager of F&C's new Russian Investment Company SICAV.
She said GDP growth was likely to come in around 2.0-3.0 percent next year, and telecoms and utility stocks would be a direct play on that growth.

"Russia is the last large emerging market in the world," she said. "Investors with a two- to 10-year time horizon are going to do extremely well...the market is going to keep going up in multiples of 100 in the years to come."
Although at $12 million the fund is tiny by the standards of rivals run by Templeton or Barings Asset Management, Knight says its small size makes it more nimble than its giant rivals.
"If you have a fund that is $100 million plus, you can't do anything discreetly in the market," she said. "This is good seed money."
She envisaged expansion to around $50 million, a size she considers attainable within the next six months, after marketing in Sweden, Switzerland and the United States later this year.

Informally launched on June 27, the fund is unusual for a Russian vehicle in being open ended, enabling it to buy and sell on a daily basis, Knight said. Unlike closed funds, open ended funds do not require investors to commit to the fund for a fixed length of time.
The F&C fund also aims to be fully invested in Russian equities traded on local Russian exchanges and will invest in ADRs. It will be listed in Luxembourg.
While the fund aims to outperform the IFC's World Index, Knight said the Moscow Times Index was a more comparable guide.
With some 49 percent of its assets invested in oil and gas, 27 percent in power utilities and 10 percent in telecoms, the Moscow Times index covers the same areas as the F&C fund.
But Knight said her fund was underweight in oil and gas, and overweight in power and telecoms, in comparison.
She did not rule out expanding into smaller firms.
"The next six to 12 months would be the time to look at lesser known companies, depending on the market's development," she said.
She dismisses suggestions the fund has already missed the rally in Russian stocks.
"You may have missed the first 20 or 30 percent, but we believe the market will keep going up in multiples of 100 percent in the next year," she said.
Knight has been at F&C since early 1995 and also manages a Polish and an east European fund. Prior to that, she managed east European and Turkish funds for Morgan Stanley, she said.

The fund is charging a 1.5-percent management fee. A performance fee of 15 percent of the excess of outperformance of the IFC Clobal Composite Total Return Index will also be levied. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
